cells.tense: You are deciding by method right now, and the deciding is settling things.
cells.ask: Before you research the next decision, write one line on what you already sense about it. Then let the work start from there.
cells.core:
You're in the middle of the work and it shows. Not waiting for a sign or a feeling to make the call — you've done the reading, you've sat with it, and the next step is visible in the doing. That's rare. Most people stall right where you move.

Sensing what matters and working it out run together in you. You don't need to know why something matters before you can tell that it does, and the method you keep — the notes, the hours, the steady quiet attention — is how that sense gets to land in a real decision. What this is free to feed next: the next hard thing you already suspect you could take on. The balance costs nothing to keep except the willingness to keep going when the result isn't visible yet.
cells.sheetLine: You decide by method, and the method is serving you.
cells.place: where the knowing comes before the figuring out

cells.tense: You will have figured this whole thing out before it has had a chance to happen.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been working out and let it stand, unfinished, until someone else's answer changes the shape. Notice what that does.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of the moment, building the case for something that isn't here yet. The rigor is real, but right now it's aimed at a future you're trying to write in advance — testing angles, defending positions, being ready before the moment asks. The thing you're preparing to defend hasn't asked to be defended.

What you're good at — sensing what to attend to — is being spent on rehearsal, not on the room you're in. The method is still the method; it's just leaning into a wall that may not be there. The other side of this is practice that flows without force, where the solitude of long attention connects instead of isolating. That's available now, not after the answer comes. Start there.
cells.sheetLine: You're solving a problem before it has happened.
cells.place: where the knowing comes before the figuring out

cells.tense: You knew what to attend to, and you left that room a long time ago.
cells.ask: Put the study materials down for one afternoon and have a conversation about something with no practical use. Let what matters show up on its own.
cells.core:
You can still feel when something deserves your full attention — a problem, a person, a detail worth turning over. But you've stopped trusting that, or stopped acting on it. The practice thinned out into a habit you keep at arm's length, and now the quiet that used to focus you just feels like a bare room.

It isn't that you've lost the ability to see what matters. It's that you've stopped feeding the part of you that can tell what's fair to yourself — what deserves your effort and what doesn't. That's not a thought problem. It's a giving-and-receiving problem, and it turns back on when you let something come at you without calculating what it costs. Small exchange, not grand gesture.
cells.sheetLine: You still know what matters. You've stopped letting that knowing act.
cells.place: where the knowing comes before the figuring out

cells.tense: You are deciding this already, and you are calling it just how things work.
cells.ask: Name one decision you made this week that came from what you already sensed, not from what you researched. Say it out loud, plainly, as yours.
cells.core:
It's running. The attention, the method, the way you sort the important from the loud — it's happening, and you're talking about it like something that just occurred. 'It needed doing.' 'That's the sensible thing.' The judgment that steers all of it is yours, and you haven't said so, even to yourself.

What you have is the ability to see what matters before you can explain why, and you've handed the credit to the task, the schedule, the obviousness of it all. That's the smallest lie a person can tell, and it costs the most, because the thing you're best at stays someone else's. The earlier form of this — before the method got so automatic — was wonder. It's still available. Look at one thing you've become precise about and let it be interesting again.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one deciding. Say so, once.
cells.place: where the knowing comes before the figuring out

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the rigor is 'ruling' — the record's language of governance — which would flatter the person into a Judge they never chose to be; the reader could fairly say 'I'm not governing anything, I just do the work carefully.' The ask survives being wrong at every status because each one is a small doable act that teaches by doing — the person learns what they already attend to and what they've been ignoring. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line suggesting this is a destiny of authority rather than a habit of attention the person can put down.
